public_rationale: On 2024-07-28, Marcus wrote that the current, short-term investment climate was hugely biased against genuine novelty and outside-the-box thinking. This is a judgment about what investors prefer. Neither 'genuine novelty' nor 'outside the box thinking' has an agreed measure. The claim also gives no baseline for what an unbiased split of funding would be. Crunchbase data published on 2025-01-07 show that almost a third of 2024 AI funding went to foundation model companies (e1). That shows where the money went. It cannot show whether the split was biased against novel ideas.
limitations: The Crunchbase figure covers all of 2024 and was published after the post. The claim is about the climate in July 2024.
Only one funding source was consulted.
A narrower version of the claim could be checked, such as the share of funding going to non-LLM or neurosymbolic approaches. The claim does not state one.
